mechanism: Hydrochlorothiazide can cause hyperuricemia and impair renal function, potentially increasing ethambutol toxicity and reducing its renal clearance, while ethambutol may cause hyperuricemia and gout exacerbation.
action: Monitor renal function, uric acid levels, and ethambutol serum concentrations; assess for gout symptoms and vision changes; consider alternative antihypertensive if hyperuricemia develops.
